results.title: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over a field $K$ of characteristic zero, and let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Lie module over $L$ and $K$. Then every Lie submodule $W$ of $M$ has a complement: there is a Lie submodule $U$ of $M$ with $W \cap U = 0$ and $W + U = M$.

results.title: Levi decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field $K$ of characteristic zero, and let $\operatorname{rad}(L)$ be its radical, the largest solvable ideal of $L$. Then there is a semisimple Lie subalgebra $S$ of $L$ (a Levi factor) such that $L = \operatorname{rad}(L) \oplus S$ as $K$-vector spaces, that is, $\operatorname{rad}(L) + S = L$ and $\operatorname{rad}(L) \cap S = 0$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 11.68 (ordered groups with three conjugacy classes)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every fully ordered group $G$ there are a fully ordered group $H$ with exactly three conjugacy classes and a strictly increasing homomorphism $G \to H$ (an order-preserving embedding). Here a fully ordered group is a group with a linear order $\le$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ and $ac \le bc$ for all $a$, $b$, $c$.

results.title: Not every fully ordered group embeds in one with three conjugacy classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a fully ordered group $G$ such that for every fully ordered group $H$ with exactly three conjugacy classes, no homomorphism $G \to H$ is strictly increasing. Here a fully ordered group is a group with a linear order $\le$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ and $ac \le bc$ for all $a$, $b$, $c$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 11.68 is negative.

results.title: Two elements generate a dense subgroup of a connected semisimple Lie group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every connected real analytic Lie group $G$ whose Lie algebra is semisimple contains two elements $a$ and $b$ such that the subgroup of $G$ generated by $a$ and $b$ is dense in $G$. In particular, for connected groups the number 4 in Problem 90 of the Scottish Book (four elements generating a dense subgroup) can be lowered to 2.

results.title: Hyers' theorem (Hyers–Ulam stability of the Cauchy equation)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `f : E → F` between real normed spaces, with `F` complete, satisfies `‖f (x + y) - f x - f y‖ ≤ δ` for all `x, y`, then there is an additive map `A : E →+ F` with `‖f x - A x‖ ≤ δ` for all `x`. The bound `δ` is sharp: for `f x = x + c` on `ℝ` the defect is `‖c‖` and the best additive approximant is the identity, at distance exactly `‖c‖`.

results.title: Uniqueness in Hyers' theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two additive maps both within `δ` of the same `f` are equal: their difference is additive, hence `n`-homogeneous, while staying bounded by `2 * δ`.

results.title: Hyers–Ulam stability of Jensen's functional equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the midpoint (Jensen) defect `‖f ((1/2) • (x + y)) - (1/2) • (f x + f y)‖` is `≤ δ` for all `x, y`, then `f` is within `4 * δ` of an additive map plus the constant `f 0`. The factor `4` comes from doubling the two Jensen estimates at `(x + y, 0)` and `(x, y)`.

results.title: Continuous Hyers–Ulam stability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `f` is continuous at `0` (in particular if `f` itself is continuous), the additive approximant from Hyers' theorem is continuous, hence a continuous real-linear map. The proof: continuity of `f` at `0` bounds `f` on a small ball, so the approximant is bounded on that ball, and an additive map bounded on a ball is continuous at `0` by the dyadic scaling argument.

results.title: Rohrbach's symmetric basis theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of natural numbers and $a$ a natural number with $\{a - x : x \in A\} = A$, where $a - x$ denotes truncated subtraction ($a - x = 0$ when $x > a$). If every natural number $m \le a$ is a sum $x + y$ of two elements $x, y \in A$, then every natural number $m \le 2a$ is such a sum.

results.title: Subset sums with a bounded number of terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $\alpha, \beta$ and a finite subset $A$ of an additive commutative monoid $G$, the set $\Sigma^{\beta}_{\alpha}(A)$ is the union of the restricted sumsets $m^{\wedge} A$ over $\alpha \le m \le |A| - \beta$, that is, the set of sums $\sum_{b \in B} b$ over subsets $B \subseteq A$ with $\alpha \le |B| \le |A| - \beta$. Here $|A| - \beta$ is read as $0$ when $\beta > |A|$.

results.title: Sequence with prescribed multiplicities
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a type, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $A = (a_0, \dots, a_{k-1})$ a $k$-tuple of elements of $G$ and $\bar t = (t_0, \dots, t_{k-1})$ a $k$-tuple of natural numbers. The sequence $(A, \bar t)$ is the finite multiset of elements of $G$ obtained by taking $t_i$ copies of $a_i$ for each $i < k$; an element $x \in G$ thus occurs $\sum_{i : a_i = x} t_i$ times.

results.title: Erdős Problem 923 on triangle-free subgraphs of large chromatic number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition asserts that for every natural number $n$ there is a natural number $k$ such that every simple graph $G$, on any vertex set, whose chromatic number is at least $k$ has a triangle-free subgraph $H$ on the same vertex set whose chromatic number is at least $n$. Chromatic numbers may be infinite.

results.title: Rödl's theorem on triangle-free subgraphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ there is a natural number $k$ such that every simple graph $G$, on any vertex set, whose chromatic number is at least $k$ has a triangle-free subgraph $H$ on the same vertex set whose chromatic number is at least $n$. Chromatic numbers may be infinite.

results.title: Reachability by a chain of friends
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $c$ assign to each person $i$ among $N$ people a set $c(i)$ of people, the friends of $i$. A person $b$ is reachable from a person $a$ if there are $m \ge 0$ and people $p_0 = a, p_1, \dots, p_m = b$ such that for each $j < m$, $p_j$ is a friend of $p_{j+1}$ or $p_{j+1}$ is a friend of $p_j$.

results.title: Assignments that connect everyone
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $c$ assign to each person $i$ among $N$ people a set $c(i)$ of people, the friends of $i$. The assignment $c$ connects all $N$ people when, for all people $a$ and $b$, there are $m \ge 0$ and people $p_0 = a, p_1, \dots, p_m = b$ such that for each $j < m$, $p_j$ is a friend of $p_{j+1}$ or $p_{j+1}$ is a friend of $p_j$.

results.title: Probability that a random $k$-out assignment connects everyone
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $N$, $P_{kN}$ is the number of assignments that give each of $N$ people a set of exactly $k$ friends other than themselves and connect all $N$ people, divided by the number of all assignments that give each person a set of exactly $k$ friends other than themselves. When there is no such assignment, $P_{kN} = 0$.

results.title: Connectivity threshold for random $k$-out friendship graphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $N$, let $P_{kN}$ be the proportion of the assignments giving each of $N$ people exactly $k$ friends other than themselves that connect all $N$ people. Then $P_{kN} \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$ for every $k \ge 2$, and $P_{1N} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$.
